_comment: CCV event schema -- the single source of truth for §1's per-instruction
event stream. tools/gen-event-schema.py generates the C++ header and the
SystemVerilog header from THIS FILE; neither is edited by hand, and §9's
requirement that names be mechanically consistent across the two languages
is satisfied by construction rather than by discipline.
WHAT IS AND IS NOT DECIDED HERE. §8 is explicit that the taxonomy is a
MECHANISM (Stage 1c) plus CONTENT that populates later, from two different
places: load-bearing events fall out of the Stage 2 interface grill-me,
arbitration-sensitive events per block at Stage 4a. So the events below are
a seed set, drawn only from the examples §1 itself names, and every one is
marked provisional. Closing the list is Stage 2's job and Stage 4a's, not
this file's.
The two CLASSES, by contrast, are decided, and the split is the point.
§1: load-bearing events must match exactly and any divergence is a bug;
arbitration-sensitive events are only comparable if the timing model's
arbiter is faithful to RTL's down to tie-break rules.

LOAD-BEARING CONTENT IS NOW POPULATED, at Stage 2 as §8 said it would be: EV_CH_XFER plus the 40-channel list in schema/interfaces.json. The per-instruction events above remain as the finer-grained view; a channel transfer is the interface-defined one.

load_bearing.description: Architectural-state-affecting, or an interface transaction. Must match exactly between timing model and RTL; any divergence is a bug.

arbitration_sensitive.description: Outcome depends on an arbiter's algorithm including tie-breaks. Comparable only against a faithful arbiter model, not a statistically plausible one.
arbitration_sensitive.correlation: OPEN -- see open item 4. Exact match if the arbiter model is faithful to tie-breaks; otherwise a stated tolerance, and correlation becomes a judgement call each run. This choice constrains how the schema records these events, so it wants settling before the content lands.

units._comment: Track identifiers -- one track per block in the Perfetto view. DERIVED from params/blocks.json, which is the closed partition, rather than listed here: a second list would disagree with the first, and this one is read by every emit site. UNIT_UNKNOWN and UNIT_TESTBENCH are not blocks and are fixed at 0 and 1; block ids follow in the partition's order. Regenerating after a partition change renumbers them and moves the schema hash, which is the intended loud failure -- a trace captured under the old numbering must not silently read as the new one.

events.name: EV_DECODE
events.doc: An instruction is decoded. First event of an instruction's life; establishes its uid for every later event.

events.name: EV_DISPATCH
events.doc: Instruction leaves the front end for the back end.

events.name: EV_ISSUE
events.doc: Instruction is selected by the arbiter and issues. §1 names issue cycle as the canonical arbitration-sensitive event: an oldest-ready model and a priority-encoder tie-break diverge on every tie, permanently, and it looks exactly like a bug.

events.name: EV_WAKEUP
events.doc: An operand became ready. Paired with EV_ISSUE it gives §1's wakeup-to-issue latency.

events.name: EV_WARP_SELECT
events.doc: Two-tier SMT warp-select outcome, including which warps were eligible but not chosen -- a losing candidate is what makes a tie-break diff meaningful.

events.name: EV_MEM_REQ
events.doc: Memory request leaves the core. Load-bearing despite memory being testbench-side (§2): §2 is explicit that interface assertions at that boundary matter MORE than elsewhere, being the one place the design meets a model nobody will ever validate.

events.name: EV_MEM_RSP
events.doc: Memory response returns to the core.

events.name: EV_RETIRE
events.doc: Instruction retires and commits architectural state. The event ccv-sim's functional oracle is checked against.

events.name: EV_BARRIER_ARRIVE
events.doc: A warp arrives at a barrier. Arrive/wait is already a split transaction (§2), so the two halves are separate events.

events.name: EV_BARRIER_RELEASE
events.doc: A barrier epoch completes and its waiters are released.

events.name: EV_CH_XFER
events.doc: A transaction crossed a channel boundary. THE load-bearing event: §1 says decode, dispatch, retire and memory request/response ARE interface transactions, and the block-level grill-me made every one of them a credited channel. So the 40-channel list is the load-bearing event list, and one event type with the channel as a discriminator covers it -- emitted by the shared credit checker, so every boundary emits identically and no block can drift from the schema.

events.name: EV_ID_LINK
events.doc: An instruction is re-executed under a NEW id, linked to the old. Squash and replay are central to this machine -- branch recovery, load replay, demotion restore -- and a reused id would show one instruction with overlapping lifetimes instead of the replay. Arbitration-sensitive because whether a replay happens can depend on contention (load replay), so model and RTL may legitimately differ on it.

_comment: Every event's instr_uid (interface decisions, 2026-09-24). TRACE-ONLY:
carried beside a message in a sideband that exists only under
CCV_TRACE, never in the RTL payload struct, so synthesis never sees it.
rob_tag cannot serve: it does not exist before rename, it is reused
after retirement, and the control channels have none.

seq.doc: 32-bit monotonic. instr: assigned at fetch. txn: the owning instruction's seq if `owned`, else from a separate transaction counter. none: 0.

sub.doc: Sub-index for one instruction's many transactions (a page-split access), so the view nests them under the instruction rather than showing peers. 0 = unnested.

owned.doc: txn only: seq names the owning instruction, and the transaction nests under it.

class.doc: What the id identifies; most channels are not per-instruction at all.
